To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) developmental jobs are characterized by a variety of components, (2) the degree to which these components are present in a job is related to learning outcomes, and (3) the degree to whch these components are present is related to the developmental challenge associated with a job.
the developmental potential of managerial jobs can be described by a set of components that reflect both the learning opportunities and outcomes that can be expected from a particular job.

the developmental challenge of a job is related to the type and amount of learning that will be experienced by the job incumbent and that developmental challenge can be assessed through the use of a job analysis questionnaire, the Developmental Challenge Questionnaire (DCQ).
In summary, our research is concerned with
how organizations can use their succession planning systems to develop managers.
the question of whether the developmental components of a job can be assessed in a selection process.
the relationship between management selection and management development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for the effectiveness of management development programs is mixed and that there is little agreement about the best way to develop managers.

, while the developmental challenge framework provides a basis for assessing the developmental potential of jobs and for matching individuals with jobs, it cannot be used as an absolute criterion for making job assignments.
the evidence for the effectiveness of management development is not strong enough to justify the large sums spent on this activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for understanding the developmental challenge of managerial jobs and have demonstrated that the framework has utility in selection and succession planning.

the more a job has the developmental challenge components of variety, complexity, autonomy, and responsibility, the more likely it is to be a learning experience and the more likely it will lead to learning outcomes.
the more we know about the job, the better we are able to predict the performance of the person on the job.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developmental challenge framework offers a useful lens for understanding how management jobs vary in the degree to which they provide opportunities to learn.
the selection and development functions are inextricably linked.
developmental assignments can provide a powerful way to develop managers, but that the potential for development depends on the type and degree to which the assignment provides a stretch.
